_meta.note: Distinct entries only; all untested. Values in Munsell N and OKLab L (L* = 116*L - 16 for neutrals). Rules labelled in VALUE_AND_NOTAN.md / EDGE_CONTROL.md / SHAPE_LANGUAGE.md.

tonal_compositions.name: Dark subject on light ground, focal at max contrast
tonal_compositions.purpose: Make a dark product (black/tortoise acetate) read instantly as a silhouette.
tonal_compositions.how: Ground N8-N9 (OKLab L 0.83-0.95), subject N1-N3 (L <= 0.40); the darkest dark of the frame touches the lightest light only at the hero edge (e.g. top rim against white); shadow under the frame N6, soft; no other dark object larger than 5% of the frame.
tonal_compositions.limits: Light metal or clear frames vanish on a light ground; flat if the subject has no internal highlight (add one specular).

tonal_compositions.name: Light subject on dark ground
tonal_compositions.purpose: Make silver/gold metal, clear or light acetate frames glow.
tonal_compositions.how: Ground N1-N3 (L <= 0.40), subject highlights N8-N9.5; rim or edge light defines the silhouette; keep ground one value group (no bright props); low key overall.
tonal_compositions.limits: Dark frames disappear; reflections on lenses must be controlled (dark environment helps).

tonal_compositions.name: Subject with both lights and darks on a mid-grey ground
tonal_compositions.purpose: Separate a subject that contains both extremes (tortoiseshell + clear lens, face with dark frame) from the ground.
tonal_compositions.how: Ground N5 +/- 0.5 (L 0.53-0.62); subject spans N1 to N9 so both its darks and lights separate from the ground; ground stays one flat or gently graded value.
tonal_compositions.limits: Mid grey can feel dull; needs colour or texture interest elsewhere.

tonal_compositions.name: Low key with one light pool
tonal_compositions.purpose: Drama, intimacy, night-shop mood with an unmistakable focal point.
tonal_compositions.how: 70%+ of area N1-N3; one pool of light (soft falloff) covering 10-20% of frame lands on the focal object; brightest highlight (N9+) inside the pool only; mean L < 0.38.
tonal_compositions.limits: Crushed shadows lose detail (keep <= 2% at L near 0 unless graphic); story needs one readable silhouette outside the pool if two characters.

tonal_compositions.name: High key with a single dark accent
tonal_compositions.purpose: Airy, gentle, hopeful images where the one dark shape is the story.
tonal_compositions.how: Mean L > 0.72; 85-95% light group; the dark group (2-10%) is the focal figure/object; p2 <= 0.45 so a real accent exists; text sits on the empty light area.
tonal_compositions.limits: If the accent is too faint (thumb32 rms < 0.08) the image reads as washed out (observed on light charcoal slides).

tonal_compositions.name: Backlit two-value silhouette
tonal_compositions.purpose: Read pure gesture and shape; mystery, nostalgia, sunset.
tonal_compositions.how: Background N8-N9.5 (sky/window), subject N0.5-N2 with no fill; silhouette must carry identity (arms off the body, glasses in profile or 3/4 so the frame shows); only a thin rim allowed inside the shape.
tonal_compositions.limits: No product detail survives - use as story/emotion frame, not as the product hero; overlaps merge silhouettes.

tonal_compositions.name: Two masses split on a diagonal, focal on the boundary
tonal_compositions.purpose: Dynamic composition with a natural focal line where light meets dark.
tonal_compositions.how: One large light mass and one large dark mass divided by a diagonal (window light, shadow edge); the focal object straddles the boundary so it gets counterchange (light part on dark, dark part on light).
tonal_compositions.limits: Boundary must not cut through a face/frame awkwardly; two equal masses feel static - make one ~60%.

tonal_compositions.name: Dark foreground frame around a lit middle
tonal_compositions.purpose: Push depth and point the eye inward (doorway, foliage, shop shelf in foreground).
tonal_compositions.how: Foreground framing shapes N1-N3, soft-edged and low detail; middle ground lit N6-N8 holds the subject; value step frame->subject >= 0.25 L.
tonal_compositions.limits: Heavy frames feel claustrophobic; in 9:16 keep the subject inside the UI safe zone.

tonal_compositions.name: Three planes stepping lighter into distance
tonal_compositions.how: Foreground darkest and highest contrast (N2-N4 with accents), middle ground N5-N6, background N7-N8 with lowest contrast; each plane one value group; the subject in the plane with the highest contrast.
tonal_compositions.limits: Fails at night or indoors without haze; avoid putting the subject in the far plane.

tonal_compositions.name: Light foreground against dark distance
tonal_compositions.purpose: Night or interior scenes where light falls near the camera.
tonal_compositions.how: Foreground lit N7-N8 (lamp, shop counter), background falls to N1-N3; subject in the lit plane; distant lights as tiny N9 accents (keep them small to avoid competing).
tonal_compositions.limits: Distant bright signs steal focus - blur or dim them.

tonal_compositions.name: Compressed mid-key (fog / soft charcoal) with one full-range spot
tonal_compositions.purpose: Soft memory or dream mood that still has a focal point.
tonal_compositions.how: Whole image within N4-N7 (L p2-p98 span 0.30-0.45) except the focal area, which alone gets N2 and N9 accents; edges soft everywhere except focal.
tonal_compositions.limits: Without the full-range spot it reads as a failed exposure; poor at thumbnail size if the spot is small.

tonal_compositions.name: Counterchange along a figure
tonal_compositions.purpose: Keep a long figure readable against a ground that changes value (wall then window).
tonal_compositions.how: Where the ground is light the figure edge is dark, where the ground is dark the figure edge is light (rim, lit sleeve); plan the switch points in the notan sketch.
tonal_compositions.limits: Needs planned lighting; random switching looks noisy.

tonal_compositions.name: Reserved one-value text band
tonal_compositions.purpose: Give the HTML text layer a calm, single-value ground in posts and carousels.
tonal_compositions.how: Reserve the top third (house style) or a band as one value group with edge density <= 0.03; text value contrasts with the band at >= 4.5:1 (body) / 3:1 (large) per WCAG; image values carry the story elsewhere.
tonal_compositions.limits: Strict bands can look templated; scrims must match the image key.

edge_control_examples.name: One hard, max-contrast edge at the focal point
edge_control_examples.purpose: Anchor the eye with the strongest found edge.
edge_control_examples.how: Pick one edge (e.g. upper rim of the frame against skin/ground) to be the only edge that is both sharp (<= 2 px transition at 1080 px) and max delta-L; everything else firm/soft.
edge_control_examples.limits: Rule of thumb, untested; competing faces/text can still win attention.

edge_control_examples.name: Lose shadow-side edges into a dark ground
edge_control_examples.purpose: Unify masses and calm the image by merging shadow side with background.
edge_control_examples.how: Where the shadow side of a form meets a ground of similar value (delta-L < 0.05), drop the edge (no outline, no rim); keep the lit side firm.
edge_control_examples.limits: Never lose edges of the identity parts (hand holding glasses, the frame itself).

edge_control_examples.name: Rim light to find an edge against a dark ground
edge_control_examples.purpose: Separate a dark subject from a dark background without lifting the whole value.
edge_control_examples.how: Back/side light producing a thin N8-N9 rim on the silhouette at the focal side; rim width 1-4 px at 1080 px; leave the far side lost.
edge_control_examples.limits: Rim on every edge looks cut out; reflections on lenses may increase.

edge_control_examples.name: Photographic depth-of-field falloff
edge_control_examples.purpose: Make the subject sharpest and the rest progressively simpler.
edge_control_examples.how: Prompt '85mm, f/1.8, shallow depth of field, the glasses in razor-sharp focus'; or HTML: background layer blur 1-3 px at 1080 px with a radial mask growing from the focal point.
edge_control_examples.limits: Too much blur reads fake or hides context; blur on line art looks wrong (use line weight/lightness instead).

edge_control_examples.name: Background lines continue through the lens (X-junctions)
edge_control_examples.purpose: Make empty cutout lenses read as glass.
edge_control_examples.how: Lines and edges behind the lens (table edge, window frame) continue through it with a small value/tint shift and slight offset; add one soft reflection band; never leave the lens fully transparent with no change.
edge_control_examples.limits: Strong mirror coatings break continuity on purpose - then the reflection carries the read.

edge_control_examples.name: Line-weight ladder for pencil/charcoal line art
edge_control_examples.purpose: Give line art depth and hierarchy without shading.
edge_control_examples.how: At 1080 px: silhouette 3-5 px, interior creases 1.5-2.5 px, texture/hatching 0.75-1.2 px; thicker on the shadow/under side (light upper-left), thinner with distance and high curvature; max:min <= 4:1.
edge_control_examples.limits: Derived from graphics method + expert observation, not a perception test; uniform weight is right for vector/ligne-claire styles.

edge_control_examples.name: Clean T-junctions at overlaps, tapered free ends
edge_control_examples.purpose: Make depth order unambiguous in line drawings.
edge_control_examples.how: The farther line stops exactly at the nearer contour (no gap, no crossing); free line ends taper; contours end where a smooth form turns away; avoid tangents (shift shapes to overlap or separate clearly).
edge_control_examples.limits: AI line art often crosses or gaps lines - check at 100%.

edge_control_examples.name: Draw contours and creases, never shadow borders
edge_control_examples.purpose: Keep line art readable and avoid false object boundaries.
edge_control_examples.how: Lines only on occluding contours and creases (the lines most artists agree on); shadows are tone/hatching without an outline; interior lines only where shading changes fast.
edge_control_examples.limits: Graphic styles (cel shading) can outline shadow shapes deliberately as a style.

edge_control_examples.name: Broken/lifted line on the light side
edge_control_examples.purpose: Suggest light hitting a form in pure line art.
edge_control_examples.how: Interrupt the contour (gaps 2-6% of the contour length) or thin it to near-zero where light hits (upper-left); keep the shadow-side contour continuous and heavier.
edge_control_examples.limits: Gaps at joints/fingers read as errors; keep gaps on smooth long contours.

edge_control_examples.name: Background lines lighter, not just thinner
edge_control_examples.purpose: Push line-art backgrounds back while keeping place information.
edge_control_examples.how: Draw scene lines in a lighter grey (e.g. ink at 40-60% opacity) and fewer of them; figures in full INK; place is still readable from structural lines.
edge_control_examples.limits: Too faint backgrounds look unfinished at thumbnail size.

edge_control_examples.name: Feathered cutout edge + contact shadow
edge_control_examples.purpose: Avoid the pasted 'sticker' look when compositing real frame cutouts.
edge_control_examples.how: Feather cutout edge 0.5-1 px, match blur to the background plane at that depth, add a contact shadow darkest at touching points; keep the frame's own detail sharp.
edge_control_examples.limits: Over-feathering softens the product - the frame must stay the sharpest object.

shape_language_examples.name: Round-dominant design for warmth
shape_language_examples.purpose: Make characters, mascots and calm promo layouts read friendly and safe at a glance.
shape_language_examples.how: Primary shapes rounded (circle/ellipse/soft rectangle), corners radius >= 15% of the shape's short side; angular shapes only as small accents; strongest at glance-speed viewing.
shape_language_examples.limits: Effect is moderate (g ~0.39) and smaller for experts and spatial designs; can feel childish if overused.

shape_language_examples.name: Angular accent for energy/tension
shape_language_examples.purpose: Add energy, alertness or conflict without implying danger by default.
shape_language_examples.how: Introduce triangles/diagonals/sharp corners on 10-20% of shapes (action lines, a pointed scarf end, a diagonal shelf); keep the hero shape cleaner.
shape_language_examples.limits: Evidence links angularity to negative association implicitly, not to avoidance; context decides.

shape_language_examples.name: Big-medium-small shape hierarchy
shape_language_examples.purpose: Make a character or prop readable at thumbnail size and interesting up close.
shape_language_examples.how: One primary mass (~60%), secondary pieces (~30%), tertiary details (~10%); test at 32/64 px that only the primary reads, at 256 px secondary.
shape_language_examples.limits: Ratios are craft, not measured; product frames must keep their true shape.

shape_language_examples.name: Duo with contrasting primary silhouettes (Mint & Tao)
shape_language_examples.purpose: Tell two faceless characters with identical heads apart by body shape alone.
shape_language_examples.how: Mint = short, round, bundled mass (oversized sweater); Tao = tall, narrow vertical rectangle (long coat) + scarf line; plus value contrast (light vs charcoal); check: height-normalised silhouette IoU < 0.75 and aspect ratios differing >= 15%.
shape_language_examples.limits: Thresholds derived, untested; seasonal costume changes must keep the primary shapes.

shape_language_examples.name: Echo the frame shape in the setting
shape_language_examples.purpose: Tie the scene to the product for unity.
shape_language_examples.how: Repeat the frame's dominant shape 2-3 times in the scene at different scales (round frame -> round window, pebbles, lamp); keep the frame distinct by value and sharpness.
shape_language_examples.limits: Too many echoes camouflage the product.

shape_language_examples.name: Break the shape pattern at the focal point
shape_language_examples.purpose: Use pop-out: the odd shape gets looked at.
shape_language_examples.how: Repeat one shape family across the field (five round frames, round shelves) and place one different shape (a square frame) at the focal spot.
shape_language_examples.limits: Only works if the repetition is clear; too many odd ones cancel out.

shape_language_examples.name: Geometric product on organic setting (or the reverse)
shape_language_examples.purpose: Separate the hero by shape family contrast.
shape_language_examples.how: Square/rectangular titanium frame on leaves, sand or fabric; or organic tortoiseshell on a hard geometric counter; keep values distinct too.
shape_language_examples.limits: If values match, shape contrast alone may not separate at thumbnail size.

shape_language_examples.name: Line of action carries emotion for faceless figures
shape_language_examples.how: Choose one C/S/I curve per figure: C curling in = sad/anxious, C leaning forward = caring/interested, I upright = calm/confident, S = relaxed/playful; two figures' lines facing each other = connection; prompt with actions, not 'dynamic pose'.
shape_language_examples.limits: Craft convention; mannequin prompts default to stiff I poses.

shape_language_examples.name: Negative space between figures as emotional distance
shape_language_examples.purpose: Show closeness or distance through the gap shape.
shape_language_examples.how: Design the gap between characters as a clear shape: narrow wedge = closeness, wide empty field = distance; arms off the body to open silhouettes; keep the top-third text zone as one clean negative shape.
shape_language_examples.limits: Craft convention; text zone must not create slivers along the frame edge.

shape_language_examples.name: Frame shape as mood cue (round = warm, square = competent)
shape_language_examples.purpose: Match frame choice and copy tone to the intended impression.
shape_language_examples.how: Round/oval frames with soft settings and warm copy; square/rectangular frames with structured settings and 'sharp/professional' copy; rimless for a natural, trustworthy look.
shape_language_examples.limits: Evidence is weak (N=39) for shape, medium for rimless; face-shape matching has no evidence found - present as style advice only.

shape_language_examples.name: Logo/mascot as one primary silhouette
shape_language_examples.purpose: Keep marks recognisable at favicon/clip-corner size.
shape_language_examples.how: One primary shape with clean negative space; test filled black at 32 px; no detail that disappears below 64 px; never alter partner logos.
shape_language_examples.limits: Curvature has no reliable effect on symbolic designs - choose by brand fit, not 'science'.

shape_language_examples.name: Push pose exaggeration for phone-size reading
shape_language_examples.purpose: Make body-language beats readable in a 1:1 grid or 9:16 Reel.
shape_language_examples.how: Exaggerate the key pose ~20-30% beyond natural (deeper slump, wider arms, bigger lean) and simplify the silhouette around it; hold the pose long enough in clips.
shape_language_examples.limits: Over-exaggeration breaks the calm Slowly Growing tone - keep within the series' gesture range.
